global: Losing {troop_count} men in one afternoon is a feat. Most would have the decency to stay quiet about it.
The council will hear every detail of that rout. I have already drafted the minutes, and they are not kind.
Funny how an army of {troop_count} can vanish while the banners stay so proudly raised.
Some commanders learn from defeat. Others simply call another vote and declare the outcome a victory.
Ser {player} has discovered a new way to lose a battle. Pity it cannot be recorded as a lesson.
A pity about the {troop_count} soldiers. They will be remembered at the next assembly, if only as a footnote.
Those who lead from the back should not be surprised when the front line breaks. Ask anyone who was there.
Do not mistake a retreat for strategy, whatever the herald says. The fief has noticed, and so have I.
whisper: {player}, {troop_count} dead men will make a poor argument at the next vote. I would start preparing excuses now.
I heard about the rout. Such a shame. Perhaps the council will finally ask who truly planned that march.
Do not expect sympathy from me. I warned your camp about that ridge, and you chose pride instead.
The seat you hoped to keep is already being measured by others. Consider this a courtesy, {player}.
{troop_count} soldiers, gone. I suppose someone will have to answer for the arithmetic, and it will not be me.
Feel free to blame the weather. Everyone else will blame your judgement, and they have far better memories.
If you need a friendly ear while your reputation bleeds, you know where I keep my patience. It is limited.
You will need allies after this, {player}. I suggest you stop making enemies in the same breath as losses.

global: A bad day for {player}, and a worse one for the {troop_count} who followed orders. The council will sort out the blame.
Reports of the defeat are spreading faster than the surviving soldiers. Curious how stories travel.
Losing most of one's army is hardly the end of a campaign. It is merely the start of a long audit.
{troop_count} troops withdrawn from the field. Whether that counts as strategy depends on who writes the record.
Some will call it a rout. Others will call it a lesson in humility. Both readings will be argued at length.
The fief has seen worse days. Whether {player} recovers is a question for the next assembly.
Morale is fragile after a loss like that. I expect the coming weeks will show who holds their nerve.
Defeat is never final on Ormerath, only expensive. Let us see what {player} can afford to rebuild.
whisper: {player}, I am sorry about the battle. Rebuilding {troop_count} men is slow work, but not impossible.
I have read the reports from the ridge. The details are unflattering, though not all of them are your fault.
Should you need counsel on rebuilding, I am willing to listen. Nothing comes free in these halls, however.
The council will want a reckoning. Before they ask, it might help to decide what you intend to say.
Losing that many soldiers changes the balance of every alliance you hold. Consider who now needs you more.
I will keep my opinions to myself for the moment. Once the dust settles, we can talk plainly.
Defeat stings, {player}. Do not let it persuade you to make rash promises to people who will forget them.
A rout is only a rout until the next council sits. After that it becomes a story, and stories can be rewritten.

global: {player} lost {troop_count} men on the ridge, and still held the line longer than most would. Respect is due.
Let the gossips gossip. A commander who survives a rout with the banner intact is worth backing.
Hard fortune struck {player} today. The council should remember who fought hardest before the collapse.
We lost ground and blood at the ridge, but not our honour. That counts for something in this realm.
A bruising defeat, and yet {player} is still standing. I will say so in the hall, and I will mean it.
Rebuild quickly, {player}. Our fief needs a commander who learns from a loss rather than hiding from it.
The {troop_count} who fell will be honoured in council. Their sacrifice is not wasted on those who listen.
Do not let the chatter bring you down. Defeats make good leaders, provided their allies stay loyal.
whisper: {player}, that was a brutal afternoon. I am sorry for the losses. Come and talk when you are ready to plan.
I saw what you tried at the ridge. Bad luck, nothing more. We can turn {troop_count} lost men into leverage.
Ser {player}, the council respects a commander who keeps their nerve. Let us make sure they remember that.
Between us, the vote can wait. Rest first, then we will discuss who should be seen to share the blame.
I have already spoken for you in the hall. Do not thank me yet, as favours here always carry interest.
You know I will back you. A few well-placed words and this defeat becomes a story about perseverance.
Losing {troop_count} soldiers is painful, but your allies are still here. That matters more than the ridge.
Keep your head high, {player}. The rivals who are smiling today will be asking for favours by the new moon.
